The first release of **pelicode**, a research prototype that tells you where your code may have come from.

pelicode keeps a database of the functions of published open-source packages, and checks a project, or only what a change touches, against it. It reports **similar code candidates to review**, each with the package, version, file, lines and license it was found in. It does not decide whether code was copied: similar code is no proof of copying, and copying is not always a problem.

The database holds hashes, locations and licenses, never source code.

## What it can do

- **Languages**: Go, Java, Kotlin, Python, Ruby and Rust, function by function (Tree-sitter), normalized at four levels: layout, identifiers and literals, types, structure.
- **Repositories**: PyPI, Maven Central, the Go module proxy, RubyGems and crates.io.
  - Downloads are verified against the digests the repositories publish, licenses are identified, and requests are paced.
  - `crawl --top N` fetches the best-known packages of each.
  - `crawl --updates` fetches the new versions of the packages in a database.
- **Matching**: exact matches after normalization, and similar matches through winnowing fingerprints, MinHash and LSH. Code common to many packages is left out, and so are the dependencies of the checked project, read from its lock files.
- **Checking**: directories, a git range (`--git main...HEAD`), or what is staged (`--staged`, for pre-commit hooks). The results come as text, JSON, CSV, or SARIF for GitHub code scanning.
- **Settings file**: `.pelicode.yaml` or `.pelicode.json5` in the repository.
- **Sharing databases**:
  - `pelicode snapshot` writes a copy for checking only.
  - Snapshots of the best-known 500 packages of each ecosystem are published monthly in quay.io (`quay.io/tama5/pelicode-db`).
  - `scan --db oci://quay.io/tama5/pelicode-db:pypi-latest` fetches, verifies and caches one; several can be checked at once.
- **Maintenance**: `pelicode stats` refreshes the counts of common hashes incrementally, and `pelicode clean` removes data no version refers to any more.

## Install

```sh
brew install tamada/tap/pelicode
cargo install pelicode-cli
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workdir quay.io/tama5/pelicode --help
```

Archives for Linux, macOS and Windows (x64 and arm64) are attached to this release. See the [installation guide](https://tamada.github.io/pelicode/install/) and [Getting Started](https://tamada.github.io/pelicode/getting-started/).

```sh
pelicode scan ./src --db oci://quay.io/tama5/pelicode-db:pypi-latest
```

## Known limitations

- **Defaults**: the default parameters (k, thresholds, the stop threshold) rest on preliminary observations; the evaluation planned in §11 of the [specification](https://github.com/tamada/pelicode/blob/main/.github/docs/spec.md) has not been done yet.
- **git**: `--git` and `--staged` need the `git` command (#6).
- **Rankings**: the best-known packages of Maven Central and Go are ranked by the number of repositories that depend on them, since those repositories publish no download counts.
- **Scale**: measured up to 1.3 million functions per database (§11.3 of the specification); larger databases are untried.
- **GitHub Action**: the action for pull requests lives in [tamada/pelicode-action](https://github.com/tamada/pelicode-action), with releases of its own.
